speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when these gait and limb coordination problems started, and have they been getting worse gradually or suddenly?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned the clumsiness is especially on the right side; has this weakness or incoordination been present since the symptoms started, or did it develop separately? Also, have you experienced any recent headaches, double vision, or difficulty speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Natalizumab carries a known risk for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), which can present with focal neurological deficits like your right-sided clumsiness. Have you noticed any changes in your memory, personality, or vision recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of natalizumab use and focal neurological deficits, I need to rule out PML immediately. REQUEST TEST: Brain MRI with contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain findings show lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images demonstrate multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement, combined with your history of natalizumab use, confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
